newsitem.title: USA: Chicago business leaders to study Olympics bid.
newsitem.headline: Chicago business leaders to study Olympics bid.

text.p: A group of Chicago area business leaders outlined on Thursday their plans for studying the economic feasibility of bidding on the 2008 Summer Olympics.

"We know we can host successful world-class events in Chicago," said John Bryan, chief executive officer of Sara Lee, in a news release. "The question is whether it makes sense for Chicago from an economic standpoint to proceed with a bid."
Bryan, the chairman of a business task force that will study the matter, said the study will be the "first step in a lengthy process."

According to the release, the task force, which includes the heads of several large corporations, will examine capital investment needs, projected revenues and operating costs, and the economic impact to Chicago and Illinois from hosting the games. The group is targeting June 1997 for having its recommendations in place.
Formal bids for the 2008 gamex are also being considered by Boston, Seattle and New York, according to the release.
